threads.body: Unlike the other start callbacks, `on_llm_start` is not included in `_ExecutionContext.instrument()`'s callback-manager refresh wrappers. A callback manager retained from before instrumentation (or from a previous instrumentation) can therefore dispatch a text-LLM start without the active handler, leaving its agent's inference count at zero. Add the sync and async `on_llm_start` dispatchers to the refresh list and cover retained managers as in `test_reinstrument_refreshes_direct_callback_dispatch`.

Initializing this to zero reports a definitive count even when the agent calls a model outside LangChain's LLM callbacks. For example, the `RunnableLambda(clients.infer)` pattern in `test_execution_context.py` can be classified as an agent, but its direct OpenAI call never reaches either increment and is reported as zero. Track those model calls through the shared invocation context, or avoid emitting a count when it cannot be determined reliably.

threads.body:
This counts every attempt, including retries from `with_retry` and retry/fallback middleware. Semconv defines inference as a logical call (see https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python-genai/pull/1000#discussion_r4432999152), so could we skip retries and only count the logical inference operations we already trace as inference spans?

It also counts calls we don't trace: `on_llm_start` (text-completion LLMs) and chat models without a detectable model name, which return below without a span. I'd rather not do extra work to count things we don't instrument and keep this simple. If you feel strongly they need to be in the metrics, let's instrument them for tracing too - tracked in #1023.
Can two independent model calls share the same ancestor model node, in which case, the flag would only count for the first call?
